lesson.subtitle: Lesson 17 -- I Couldn't Sleep: The Noisy Room and Could / Couldn't
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Leão | Lesson 17 -- I Couldn't Sleep
lesson.grammar_point: could and couldn't for the past

listenings.text: The worst night of my trip was in Lisbon. The hotel was beautiful, but my room was next to the elevator. I could hear the elevator all night: up, down, up, down. I couldn't sleep. At two in the morning I called the front desk, but nobody answered. I couldn't find my earplugs, so I put a pillow on my head. Terrible. In the morning I went to the desk and I said: could I have a quiet room, please? And they gave me a room on the top floor, with a view of the river. The second night I could sleep for nine hours.

When I was a child, I couldn't swim, and I was afraid of the sea. My brother could swim very well, and I was so jealous. When I was twenty, I couldn't speak English. I could say hello and thank you, and that was all. Now I can swim, and I swim in the sea every summer. And now I can speak English, not perfectly, but I can travel alone and I can talk to people. My advice? What you couldn't do before, maybe you can do now. You need to try.

extra_audio.text: At midnight my neighbors had a party. I could hear the music through the wall. I couldn't sleep, so I called the front desk. I said: Could I have a quiet room, please? In the new room I could sleep until eight.
